classification.difficultyReason: Translate the explicit twice-price relationship and purchase total into two equations, then routine substitution.

content.prompt:
Solve this problem by introducing two pronumerals and forming two simultaneous equations, even though it may be done more easily using one pronumeral.

At a clothing store, trousers cost twice as much as shirts. A businessman buys 4 shirts and 2 pairs of trousers for a total cost of $\$240$. How much does each shirt cost?

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the cost of one shirt in dollars and $y$ the cost of one pair of trousers in dollars.

$$\begin{align*}y&=2x&&\text{(1)}\\4x+2y&=240&&\text{(2)}\end{align*}$$

Substitute equation (1) into equation (2):

$$\begin{align*}4x+2(2x)&=240\\4x+4x&=240\\8x&=240\\x&=30\end{align*}$$

Each shirt costs $\$30$.

Check: $y=2\times30=60$, and $4\times30+2\times60=240$.
